title: Research epics: port-validation pipeline + autoresearch
body: Two new research epics registered 2026-06-18: (1) implementation validation pipeline = robust jax-port + audit-fw integration; (2) agentic algorithm evolution & autoresearch with xtrax+bathos. Both require NLM deep/fast research → contemplex brainstorm → spec before implementation. See backlog #2180+#2181 (IDs assigned on add).

title: xtrax consumer MCP server (xtrax-mcp) exposing RunSpec/CLI primitives
body: Gap identified 2026-07-15 while reviewing the Tyro CLI (E2/#2605) and T3 roadmap DAG (260702_03-dag-plugin-workflows.md): the Tyro CLI (plan/explain/export/run/resume/sweep, merged to main) is the only 'easy interface' surface currently tracked for xtrax consumers. It already emits machine-readable --fmt json, explicitly designed so 'the CLI is also the machine interface an autoresearch orchestrator drives' (260622_e1-signature-inference-epic.md). But nothing tracked ships xtrax's own MCP server so external consumers (not just the CLI or an in-process orchestrator) can drive RunSpec/plan/explain/run/BatchPlanner over MCP. Two adjacent-but-distinct threads exist and do NOT cover this: (1) 260609_mcp-plugin-portability.md is an ecosystem-wide draft standard (any <pkg>-mcp naming/entry-points/emit-config convention) not xtrax-specific and not yet applied to xtrax. (2) The T3 DAG (260702_xtrax-workflows-as-a-praxia-plugin-packa spec + roadmap) is entirely about praxia's rig-run DISPATCHING xtrax's Claude-PCW workflows -- the reverse direction from an xtrax-authored MCP server serving external consumers. Proposed shape: reuse the CLI's --fmt json contract as the MCP tool surface (xtrax-mcp wrapping plan/explain/run/resume/sweep/export), following the mcp-plugin-portability Layer-1/2 conventions once that standard stabilizes. Natural fit as an E2-remainder or new epic item under #2174/#2605.

title: Generic fail-loud TOML->dataclass config primitive (extract from TrainConfig/load_config)
body: Option 2 from the plegadx UX-seam audit (2026-07-15). xtrax.cli.config's TrainConfig/load_config (src/xtrax/cli/config.py) implement a fail-loud pattern -- schema_version check, required-section check, ConfigError-on-violation -- but the dataclass and validation are hardcoded to the training-run shape (model/optimizer/loss/data/seed/num_epochs) and load_config is cli-private (not in xtrax.cli.__all__). Consumer plegadx (building an inference CLI, not training) concluded they'd have to mirror this exact pattern themselves for their own InferConfig rather than reuse it. Proposal: extract the pattern into a schema-agnostic public helper (e.g. xtrax.config.load_toml_dataclass(path, required_sections=...) or similar), with TrainConfig/load_config becoming a thin consumer of it. This is real design surface (what varies per domain: required top-level keys, nested-section validation composition) -- needs a proper brainstorm/spec before implementation, unlike the load_fn formalization (idea/PR shipped same session, see xtrax.cli.__all__ change 2026-07-15) which was a zero-design-risk promotion of an already-generic primitive. Fits xtrax's stated charter as a substrate for domain libraries built on top of it.

title: Entry-points-based xtrax CLI verb registration (upstream ask, demand-gated)
body: Option 3 from the plegadx UX-seam audit (2026-07-15). xtrax.cli.registry.REGISTRY (src/xtrax/cli/registry.py) is a closed module-level dict with eager imports of xtrax's own verb modules -- its own docstring says outright 'these are xtrax's own CLI verb functions, not user code.' No plugin hook exists for a downstream package to register its own tyro-dispatched verb into the xtrax CLI. Consumer plegadx flagged this as an optional/upstream ask rather than blocking on it -- they're mirroring xtrax's dispatch pattern instead (tyro-dispatched registry, TOML->validated dataclass, fail-loud ConfigError) for their own FU-5 CLI. Proposal: importlib.metadata.entry_points(group='xtrax.cli.verbs') scanned in registry.py, merged with the built-in dict; downstream packages declare verbs via their own pyproject.toml [project.entry-points] section -- stdlib-native, so it does NOT reintroduce the custom register_verb() API the E2 brainstorm's own pre-mortem explicitly rejected on rot-surface grounds (see .praxia/docs/specs/260623_e2-auto-cli-for-xtrax-how-to-scope-and-d.md pre-mortem section). Consistent with that same pre-mortem's YAGNI discipline: this should be demand-gated on >=2 real consumers wanting to extend the xtrax CLI itself (plegadx's audit is currently the only demand signal), not built speculatively. If built, it would collapse plegadx's mirrored dispatcher into a thin registration, per their own note.
